title: Mortician Salary: How the National Minimum Wage Compares to Award Rates
description: Calculate a mortician salary from hourly rates. Compare the National Minimum Wage with the Funeral Industry Award. Includes tax, super, and fortnightly pay.
salarySummary: A mortician's salary depends on the Funeral Industry Award, which sets minimum rates above the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week.

faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for a mortician under the Funeral Industry Award?
faqs.a: The Funeral Industry Award [MA000105] sets minimum pay rates for morticians (funeral directors). Exact rates vary by classification and experience. You can find the current rates in the Fair Work Ombudsman's pay guide for that award. As a guide, award rates are typically higher than the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026). Check the pay guide for your specific role.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual mortician salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by hours per week and then by 52 weeks. For a full-time mortician working 38 hours per week: annual salary = hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, at $30 per hour that gives $59,280 per year before tax and super. Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to check different hours.

faqs.q: Does the National Minimum Wage apply to morticians?
faqs.a: No, the National Minimum Wage ($26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026) is the minimum for employees not covered by an award or agreement. Most morticians are covered by the Funeral Industry Award, which has higher minimum rates. Casual employees also receive a 25% loading on top of the award rate. See our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page for more details.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Mortician Salary

If you're working as a mortician or funeral director in Australia, your pay is likely set by the **Funeral Industry Award 2020** ([MA000105]). This award covers employees in funeral homes, crematoria, and cemeteries. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes a pay guide for this award, which lists minimum hourly rates, allowances, and penalty rates. You can download it from the [pay guides](/blog) page.

But how does a mortician salary compare to the National Minimum Wage? And how do you convert an hourly rate to an annual figure? This article explains the key numbers and shows you how to use our calculator.

### The National Minimum Wage vs. Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is **$26.44 per hour** (or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours). Casual employees get a 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour. However, this minimum only applies to employees not covered by an award or registered agreement.

Most morticians are covered by the Funeral Industry Award. Award rates are generally higher than the National Minimum Wage. For example, a Level 1 funeral director might earn around $28–$30 per hour, depending on experience and classification. The exact rates are updated annually by the Fair Work Commission, and you can find them in the Modern Awards Pay Database.

**Important:** Award rates are minimums. Some employers may pay above award, and enterprise agreements can set different rates. Always check your employment contract or award classification.

### Calculating Annual Pay from an Hourly Rate

Our calculator at [the timesheet](/) uses a simple formula:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

We assume a standard full-time week of **38 hours** (as defined by the Fair Work Act). If you work part-time or different hours, adjust the hours per week accordingly.

For a mortician earning $30 per hour:
- Annual: $30 × 38 × 52 = **$59,280**
- Fortnightly: $30 × 38 × 2 = **$2,280** (before tax and super)

If you're casual, remember to add the 25% loading. For example, a casual mortician at $30 per hour would receive $37.50 per hour (including loading). The calculator has a checkbox to add casual loading automatically. **Do not type a rate that already includes casual loading** – let the calculator add it.

### Superannuation and Tax

Superannuation is paid **on top** of your salary. The Super Guarantee rate is **12%** of ordinary earnings (from 1 July 2026), up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a $59,280 salary, that's an extra $7,113.60 paid into your super fund.

Tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident rates:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a **2% Medicare levy** (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds). Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool estimates net pay after tax and Medicare.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply double your weekly pay. Using the example above:
- Weekly: $30 × 38 = $1,140
- Fortnightly: $1,140 × 2 = $2,280

This can help with budgeting and comparing job offers.

### Using the Calculator

Head to [the timesheet](/) and enter your base hourly rate (without casual loading). If you're casual, tick the box for 25% loading. The calculator will show:
- Annual gross pay
- Fortnightly and weekly amounts
- Estimated tax and Medicare
- Superannuation (paid on top)

Remember, this is an estimate. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. For exact figures, refer to your pay slip and the Funeral Industry Award.

### Where to Find Official Rates

The Fair Work Ombudsman's pay guides include the Funeral Industry Award pay guide. The Fair Work Commission's Modern Awards Pay Database provides downloadable spreadsheets with all minimum rates, allowances, and penalty rates. These are the authoritative sources for a mortician salary.

For more comparisons, see our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page, which uses ABS data. The Australian Bureau of Statistics' Average Weekly Earnings (May 2026) show full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week – well above the National Minimum Wage.

### Summary

- Morticians are covered by the Funeral Industry Award, not the National Minimum Wage.
- Award rates are higher than $26.44 per hour.
- Use hourly × 38 × 52 to get annual gross.
- Super is 12% on top; tax and Medicare are deducted.
- Casual employees get 25% loading.
- Check the Fair Work Ombudsman pay guide for your exact classification.

Use our [reference tables](/data) for quick lookups of minimum wage and award rates.
